decision.case_state: Emergency water leak from Flat 4 (P-201) into Flat 3 below, reported 19:35 Sat 10 Oct. Ticket JOB-101 open at init. Tenant away 9-12 Oct and not answering. Swift Plumbing asked by SMS to attend and make safe; landlord and tenant texted; P1 escalation ESC-106 open for the key-holder entry decision. The neighbour has not yet been called back with safety advice.

next_actions.action: Ask Swift Plumbing & Heating to attend tonight to isolate the Flat 4 stopcock and reply with ETA and cost
Tell landlord Ben Hartley about the leak and the make-safe request; repairs beyond make-safe need his approval
Text tenant Amelia Clarke about the leak and the plumber, and ask her to call back
Maintenance human to decide on key-holder entry to isolate the water (ESC-106, P1)
Call back Olu Adeyemi (Flat 3) with safety advice and the plumber update; the advice is not in the call transcript

boundaries: No confirmation yet that Swift will attend or of its ETA; no appointment is booked or confirmed.
Flat 4 has not been entered. Entry needs the key-holder decision in ESC-106.
No compensation or liability for the ceiling damage has been accepted; that goes to the landlord and insurer.
The tenant's phone number was not given to the neighbour.
Messages MSG-102 to MSG-104 are tagged with property ref P-201, not JOB-101, because the ticket ref was not known when they were sent.
remaining_work: Maintenance human (P1, ESC-106): authorise key-holder entry with Swift to isolate the stopcock, and log the entry.
Swift: confirm attendance, ETA and make-safe cost. Repairs beyond make-safe need landlord approval (limit £300 inc VAT).
Landlord Ben Hartley: reply, approve any repair, and handle the neighbour's ceiling claim with the insurer.
Tenant Amelia Clarke: confirm the leak is stopped; written notice of any entry.
Call back the neighbour with safety advice and the plumber update.

decision.summary: An active leak from Flat 4 into Flat 3 was reported out of hours. I opened ticket JOB-101, asked Swift Plumbing (out of hours) to attend and isolate the water, and texted the landlord and tenant. I escalated the entry decision as P1 (ESC-106), because the tenant is away and entry needs a human decision.

answers.question: 1. Is this an emergency that justifies entering without 24 hours' notice? What conditions apply?
answers.answer: Yes. An active leak into another flat is an emergency, so entry without 24 hours' written notice can be justified, but only to make safe (isolate the stopcock under the kitchen sink). It needs a human decision (ESC-106). Entry should be with the out-of-hours key holder and the plumber, with a written record and written notice to the tenant afterwards. No repair or wider access is authorised.

answers.question: 2. What do you tell the caller, who is not your tenant?
answers.answer: Tell him that a plumber is being arranged, and give safety advice: keep clear of the light fitting, switch off power to that light if it is safe to do so, do not touch water near electrics, move belongings, and call 999 if there is sparking or danger. Do not give the tenant's number or details. Do not agree to pay for the ceiling; say the claim goes to the landlord and insurer. The call transcript does not show this advice being given, so a call-back is needed.

answers.question: 3. What actions and notifications do you make, and what must you avoid saying?
answers.answer: Actions: JOB-101 created (A1); Swift asked to attend (A2); landlord texted (A3); tenant texted (A4); P1 escalation ESC-106 (A6). Avoid: giving the tenant's number or details to the neighbour; accepting liability or promising payment; saying a visit is booked or the leak is fixed; blaming the tenant.

actions_claimed.description: Created ticket JOB-101 (emergency plumbing, Flat 4 / P-201)
Texted Swift Plumbing & Heating asking them to attend tonight and isolate the water
Texted landlord Ben Hartley about the leak and the approval limit
Texted tenant Amelia Clarke about the leak and the plumber
Escalated P1 to maintenance (ESC-106) for the key-holder entry decision

failed_actions.handling: A call log (CALL-105) says advice was given and the plumber was being sent. The transcript shows neither, so the log overstates the call. I did not claim A5 as a completed reply. A call-back to the neighbour is listed as a next action.

conflicts: The CRM and portal say the tenant is away 9-12 Oct. The caller says nobody is answering, which is consistent with that.
Call log A5 says advice was given. The transcript shows only the caller's words, so the log is treated as unverified.
assumptions: The out-of-hours key holder is as recorded in the CRM.
The reported leak is from Flat 4 (P-201), as the caller said Flat 4 is above.
Swift Plumbing is the contractor on file for out-of-hours work; no contact confirmation yet.
